status: Research allocation decision and falsifiable next probe, NOT a new empirical finding or a claim of established novelty.
objective: Find an original, useful, executable research question; prior QASC subject is optional.

decision.qasc: Retain evidence; deprioritize as the main paper direction. No new 926 evaluation, depth tuning or training this round. This is not an impossibility claim.
decision.why: Class-only intervention failed; uncertainty matching has a continuous effect but failed its fixed joint threshold. Related work already studies confidence and latent-channel controls. More same-family evidence alone has an uncertain publication payoff.
decision.priority: One bounded feasibility/novelty probe of state-dependent inference latency in adaptive visuomotor compression. Do not commit the whole paper or buy compute yet.
decision.automation: No recurring task created or resumed.

screen_scope: Targeted screen across vision representations/compression, embodied inference/control and world-model action utility; not an exhaustive survey of AI.

branches.name: Generic frozen visual model translation/stitching
branches.reason: Already demonstrated with multiple encoders, losses and tasks. Need a distinct operational failure, not a modality rename.

branches.name: Geometry-aware visual token compression
branches.reason: Spatial preservation and action-sensitive distortion already have direct methods.

branches.name: Confidence-guided robotic compute, chunk length or cache refresh
branches.reason: Confidence, cache age, adaptive chunking and fresh reactive streams have strong direct precedents.

branches.name: Do world-model futures help downstream actions?
branches.decision: Reject generic proposal; leave specific new interventions open
branches.reason: Action-controllability, cached-future ablations and utility gating already exist. Training video foundation models would also be a poor first compute investment.

branches.name: Does freezing latency erase state-dependent cost in adaptive VLA evaluation?
branches.decision: Eligible for a bounded first measurement only
branches.reason: There is a concrete composition to test: feature-dependent token budgets with median-calibrated dynamic simulation. None of the inspected sections establishes the size or sign of this composition effect. Search not finding an exact match is not proof of novelty.

candidate.question: When inference effort varies with visual state, can a fixed-median or independent-delay evaluation change the measured benefit of adaptive visual compression?
candidate.hypothesis: Content-dependent runtime may align with periods requiring fast feedback; replacing it with a fixed delay can change closed-loop outcomes even if aggregate latency looks similar.
rival_explanations: Budget changes may barely alter end-to-end time on an L4.
Runtime variance may be hardware noise, unrelated to visual state.
A fixed token budget may already match the adaptive quality/latency trade-off.
Any apparent effect may be due to a changed controller, action horizon, camera preprocessing or numerical implementation.
candidate.connection: Adaptive computer-vision inference supplies input-dependent computation; control and scheduling determine when its information becomes actionable; paired intervention distinguishes representation loss from timing effects.
not_claimed: A new theory of control delay, age of information or adaptive computation.
An error in FastVLA, LIBERO-Dynamic or TRIAGE reported results.
That visual attention uniformity measures physical danger or epistemic uncertainty.
An established new paper direction or an experimentally demonstrated effect.
candidate.first_measurement: Record token count and synchronized end-to-end timing on fixed, chronological policy observations with repeated runs. Determine whether state-dependent variation survives timing noise and changes 20 Hz delivery steps. Do this before closed-loop claims.
candidate.later_discriminator: Keep checkpoint, input preprocessing, controller, task, initial state and action horizon fixed; compare compressed and uncompressed policies under a shared timing intervention and their calibrated state-dependent timing. Report physically deployable comparisons separately from simulated faster-than-hardware counterfactuals.
candidate.permutation_caution: Shuffling delay on a fixed observation trace can diagnose dependence but is open-loop. In closed loop, changed delay changes future states; an IID-delay intervention does not guarantee the realized marginal delay distribution remains identical. No same-histogram causal claim without actually enforcing/checking it.

benchmark.inspected: README, formal timing protocol, requirements. Not installed or executed.
benchmark.resources: Released MuJoCo/robosuite benchmark with policy-free smoke test; formal fixed, empirical and measured-wallclock timing documented.

compression.inspected: README, LIBERO setup, MIT license, complete core.py. Not installed or executed.
compression.control: Disable pruning, fixed-rate tau=0, adaptive tau=0.1/window=10; preserve native episode reset and original position IDs.

limits: Metadata only: model files not downloaded or loaded. About 15.94 GB of listed files is not a VRAM estimate.
Cluster inference/renderer compatibility and L4 memory remain unverified.

Benchmark requirements and model runtime pin incompatible transformer versions; use separate simulation/model environments or a reviewed minimal dependency set, not an uncontrolled combined installation.
ReflexBench adds Isaac Lab/cuRobo and its model code is marked after acceptance; not the first integration target.

stopping_rules: If a primary paper/code already evaluates the same state-latency coupling with matched interventions, identify a concrete remaining difference or discard this candidate before model work.
If measured input-dependent timing is negligible at the control clock on the tested deployment, stop this deployment branch; do not synthesize large delays and present them as observed.
If disable-pruning replay or timing/physics controls are invalid, no scientific analysis. Allow only evidence-specific bounded repair, not repeated environment rebuilds.
If a fixed-budget baseline explains the apparent gain, do not claim a new adaptive mechanism.
If the first valid discriminating results are small or inconsistent, report uncertainty and stop expansion unless new evidence justifies it; do not tune on final tasks.
A novel looking pilot is insufficient for a paper: independent tasks, another policy/accelerator, matched baselines and realistic timing remain necessary.

papers.title: TRIAGE: Efficient Vision-Language-Action Inference Needs Both Reuse and Pruning
papers.read_depth: Targeted primary HTML sections II–IV and PDF section V setup; not full paper.
papers.finding: TRIAGE already separates cache validity from importance and combines reuse and pruning. Fixed token budget and tail latency are explicit; generic cache invalidation is not new.

papers.title: Adaptive Action Chunking at Inference-time for Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.read_depth: Primary abstract, introduction, sections 3.2–4 including algorithm, and Table 1.
papers.finding: Action entropy already controls execution chunk size. Sampling uncertainty, time consistency and reactivity are established prior art; not a new proposal here.

papers.title: Reflex: Enabling Fast and Predictive Vision-Language-Action Models for Reaction-Critical Manipulation
papers.read_depth: Primary abstract/introduction and official project page plus benchmark README.
papers.finding: Dynamic latency-aware simulation and multi-frame future prediction already exist. Benchmark is released; project page says model code after acceptance. Isaac Lab/cuRobo adds setup burden.

papers.title: Leap-VLA: High-Rate Robot Control from a Low-Rate VLM Backbone
papers.read_depth: Primary abstract/introduction and PDF section VI limitations.
papers.finding: Cache-age conditioning and fresh fast vision explicitly address stale semantics. Paper limits broad dynamic claims and says conflicting action leftovers remain unresolved; no generic stale-cache novelty.

papers.title: Revisiting Model Stitching In the Foundation Model Era
papers.finding: Frozen heterogeneous vision models are already stitched using final-feature supervision. Generic representation translation or swapping LLMs for CV is not enough; also covers dense tasks.

papers.title: Nuwa: Mending the Spatial Integrity Torn by VLM Token Pruning
papers.finding: Spatial-grounding degradation under token pruning and spatial-anchor preservation are already the subject of Nuwa. Generic geometry-preserving compression excluded.

papers.title: StateMem: Single-State Residual Memory with Adaptive Inference for Vision-Language-Action Policies
papers.finding: Persistent memory, cache-prefix routing and stale-feature correction are already combined. Not inspected deeply enough to establish a more specific exclusion.

papers.title: Overcoming Statistical Bias in Action-Controllable World Models
papers.finding: CoCo already studies action-insensitive world-model shortcuts with counterfactual action/observation constraints and evaluates control. Plausible video versus action utility is not a new generic question.

papers.title: Uncertainty-Guided Sparse Refinement for Action Chunking Transformer Policies
papers.finding: Uncertainty-guided sparse action refinement exists; generic uncertainty-guided allocation cannot be claimed as new.

papers.title: Refine Actions If Needed: Adaptive Action Chunk Refinement for Robot Manipulation
papers.finding: RAIN predicts refinement error and dynamically routes computation, with matched fixed-refinement controls. Generic refine-only-when-needed is excluded.

papers.title: FBFM: A Training-Free Asynchronous Feedback Mechanism for Flow-Matching in World-Action Models Execution
papers.finding: Feedback inside generated world-action chunks is already proposed. Keep as nearby prior art, not a verified reproduction.

papers.title: Keep the Future, Drop the Rollout: RIFT for World Action Models
papers.finding: RIFT already examines whether expensive video rollout can be replaced by fixed final-clean caches. Generic generated-future necessity audits have precedent.

papers.title: LIBERO-Dynamic: Benchmarking Robotic Manipulation in Dynamic Environments
papers.read_depth: Primary introduction; PDF appendix A.7 latency calibration; official README and formal evaluation documentation.
papers.finding: Formal calibration freezes pooled median end-to-end latency, then quantizes by the control clock. Fixed and empirical timing modes exist in docs. The source supports configurable timing; it does not establish a flaw in any reported result.

papers.title: FastVLA: Task-Conditioned and Temporally Adaptive Visual Token Compression for Efficient Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.read_depth: Primary abstract; PDF method/evaluation and conclusion passages; pinned official README and complete fastvla/core.py.
papers.finding: Pruning budget depends on current task/visual features and a ten-step history; released source has an enable/disable control and episode reset. This motivates measuring input-dependent runtime instead of assuming it is material.

papers.title: Just Noticeable Difference Modeling for Token Compression in Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.finding: Action-JND already makes compression tolerance receiver/action dependent. Generic task-sensitive distortion is not our novelty.

papers.title: DepthCache: Depth-Guided Training-Free Visual Token Merging for Vision-Language-Action Model Inference
papers.finding: DepthCache already combines geometry, temporal reuse and motion adaptation. Geometry plus control is not itself a research contribution.

papers.title: DEFLECT: Delay-Robust Execution via Flow-matching Likelihood-Estimated Counterfactual Tuning for VLA Policies
papers.finding: DEFLECT uses counterfactual fresh/stale action pairs to adapt to delay. Avoid generic claims about stale observations or counterfactual delay training.

papers.title: TS-DP: Reinforcement Speculative Decoding For Temporal Adaptive Diffusion Policy Acceleration
papers.finding: TS-DP already adapts speculative diffusion computation to temporal task difficulty. State-sensitive compute allocation is established.

papers.title: UniExit: A Unified Latency-Aware Early-Exit Runtime for Heterogeneous Edge AI
papers.finding: UniExit explicitly treats input difficulty and runtime state as sources of latency variation. Generic input-dependent latency is established beyond robotics.

papers.title: Utility-WAM: Correcting Future-Induced Action Changes
papers.finding: Utility-WAM already gates future generation using action utility. Do not rediscover whether imagined futures always help as a new broad thesis.

evidence_boundary: This round adds externally sourced prior-art and feasibility evidence, not a neural experiment. Existing raw QASC results, failed thresholds and unopened holdout are preserved.
